messages.content: Let's do the hotel comparison for California now. Three nights up by Santa Monica or Malibu, then five around San Diego. I need complete numbers, not teaser rates, and make sure the room actually allows all three of us.

I’ll compare July 19-22 in the northern beach area and July 22-27 in San Diego for two adults and one 12-year-old. I’ll include the exact room setup, taxes, mandatory fees, parking, cancellation terms, and practical driving times. I’ll also refresh the LAX-pickup/SAN-return car price so the split can be judged as a whole.
Right. Keep it to two combinations that are actually sensible. We don't need luxury, but I don't want a room where the third person is only implied by a photo of a sofa.

Understood. I’m excluding any rate that does not explicitly list maximum occupancy of at least three and a defined bed or confirmed sofa bed. One question before I narrow San Diego: should I weight Mission Bay and Liberty Station equally, or is one of those more useful for this trip?
Equally. We'll have the car. I care more about the total and whether the room works than a small difference in driving time.

The strongest value pair so far is the Sea View Hotel in Santa Monica followed by the Bahia Resort Hotel at Mission Bay. I’m checking the fee and cancellation language directly because both initial listings separate some charges from the nightly rate.
And compare that with something where breakfast is included if there's a decent one. Five mornings in San Diego can add up.

The alternative pair is Hampton Inn & Suites Santa Monica with Homewood Suites San Diego Airport-Liberty Station. Both include breakfast, and their selected room types explicitly accept three guests. I’m calculating both pairs on the same basis now.
Go ahead.

Combination 1, lower total: Sea View Hotel Santa Monica for three nights in a room with two double beds, maximum occupancy four. The stay is $1,332 including room tax; valet parking is $55 nightly, or $165, making the northern stop $1,497. Breakfast is not included. Cancellation is free through 6:00 p.m. Pacific on July 16; after that, the penalty is one night plus tax, quoted as $444.

Then Bahia Resort Hotel for five nights in a garden-view room with two queen beds, maximum occupancy four. The $1,845 total includes taxes and the mandatory resort fee. Self-parking is included. Cancellation is free through 4:00 p.m. Pacific on July 19; the penalty afterward is the first night, $369 including tax and fee.

The eight-night hotel-and-parking total is $3,342.
What are the practical drive times on that one? Not the optimistic map numbers.

From Sea View, Santa Monica Pier is about a 4-minute walk, and Malibu Pier is generally 35-50 minutes by car, closer to an hour in a heavy afternoon period. On the transfer day, Sea View to Bahia is roughly 2 hours 10 minutes without meaningful congestion; I would budget 3 to 3 hours 15 minutes with a lunch or fuel stop and normal Orange County traffic.

From Bahia, allow 15-25 minutes to the San Diego Zoo, 20-30 minutes to La Jolla, and 15-20 minutes to SAN when returning the car. Those ranges include ordinary daytime traffic but not a major incident.
Now the breakfast pair, same detail.

Combination 2: Hampton Inn & Suites Santa Monica for three nights in a room with two queen beds, maximum occupancy four. The room and taxes total $1,449. Valet parking is $50 nightly, adding $150, so that stop is $1,599. Breakfast is included. Free cancellation runs through 11:59 p.m. local time on July 16; canceling later costs one night, currently $483 including tax.

Homewood Suites San Diego Airport-Liberty Station is five nights in a one-bedroom suite with two queen beds in the bedroom and a listed sofa bed in the living area; maximum occupancy is six. The room and taxes total $1,940. Self-parking is $25 nightly, adding $125, for a San Diego total of $2,065. Breakfast is included. Cancellation is free through 11:59 p.m. Pacific on July 20; afterward the charge is one night plus tax, $388.

That pair totals $3,664 for eight nights including taxes and parking, $322 more than Combination 1.
For this trip, don't let free breakfast decide it. If the cheaper pair is otherwise sound, we can buy breakfast and still come out ahead. I just wanted the included option priced.

Then Combination 1 remains the better value. Its rooms explicitly accommodate three, it saves $322, and parking is already accounted for. Even allowing $45-$55 per family breakfast on five or six mornings, the difference is largely absorbed rather than turning Combination 2 into a clear financial win. Combination 2 mainly buys the larger San Diego suite and predictable breakfast, not a lower trip cost.
How do the driving times compare for the Hampton and Homewood pair? And refresh the car.

Hampton is about 5-10 minutes by car from Santa Monica Pier and 35-55 minutes from Malibu Pier. Hampton to Homewood is usually 2 hours 15 minutes in clear traffic; budget 3-3.25 hours on the Wednesday transfer. From Homewood, allow 15-20 minutes to the zoo, 20-30 minutes to La Jolla, and 5-10 minutes to SAN. It is more convenient for the airport than Bahia but not enough to offset the $322 difference by itself.

The current midsize car quote is $684 total for LAX pickup July 19 at 12:45 p.m. and SAN return July 27 at 9:45 a.m. That includes base rate, taxes, and a $96 one-way fee; it does not include fuel, tolls, optional coverage, or child equipment. The reservation is pay-later and cancellable without charge before pickup.
Put the car against both totals. Also, does three nights north and five south still make sense, or are we forcing the split because that was the first idea?

With the current $684 car quote, Combination 1 is $4,026 for hotels, parking, taxes, mandatory fees, and the rental car. Combination 2 is $4,348 on the same basis. Fuel, meals, tolls, and optional rental coverage remain outside both totals.

The three-and-five split still makes sense. Arrival day leaves only part of Sunday in Santa Monica, so three northern nights provide two full days for Santa Monica and Malibu without overcommitting to that area. Five San Diego nights provide four full days after the transfer, which is more useful if you divide time among the zoo, La Jolla, Mission Bay, and another coastal or flexible day. A four-and-four split would add a northern night while removing the flexible San Diego day, and current matching rates would not produce a meaningful saving.

I would retain Combination 1 as the price choice and Combination 2 as the space-and-breakfast alternative. Nothing has been reserved.
